assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology, from proglucagon-derived peptide identification and the insulinotropic action of the active truncated forms to long-acting agonists, has transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with cardiovascular and renal benefit signals. Importance, clarity and breadth of patient impact are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology of GLP-1 secretion and action) and Drucker (biology and translation of GLP-1 and GLP-2) are central; Mojsov's contribution on the active peptide form is part of the credit story. Knudsen's drug-development role is industrial and could be an alternative, so a three-person limit forces a hard choice. Wider foundational credit (e.g. to people outside this credited list) is something I cannot verify here.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent clinical confirmation and very large outcome trials; interpretation is stable and recognition is timely, arguably overdue given global use.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit between the discovery of the active peptide and its physiology is disputed in the literature as I recall it.
The credited list may omit key contributors, and I have not independently verified priority claims.
Whether basic discovery or drug development is the prize-worthy core is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics provided a general method to control defined cell populations with light and reshaped neuroscience and physiology, including circuit dissection and early clinical applications. The tool-plus-discovery story (channelrhodopsin) is original and has lasting, broad impact.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin identification and characterization (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg) and the neuronal implementation (Deisseroth, Boyden, with Miesenböck's earlier genetically targeted photoactivation) form a multi-party story with six credited names; any three-person split leaves out prominent contributors.
assessment.maturity: Over fifteen years of widespread, independent adoption; the method is mature. Clinical translation is still early but not necessary for recognition of the tool.
uncertainties: Strongly contested allocation among six credited people with overlapping priority claims.
Therapeutic maturity is limited beyond early retinal applications.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells, particularly CD19 CAR-T therapy, produce durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and opened a new class of living drugs. Importance and clinical impact are clear and the concept is original.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain and June drove design and clinical proof of CAR constructs with costimulation; Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell therapy and early CAR trials. Earlier receptor-chimera work (e.g. Eshhar) is not in the credited names, which complicates fair attribution.
assessment.maturity: Approved products since 2017 with multi-year follow-up; maturity is good, though toxicity, solid tumour limits and long-term outcomes continue to evolve.
uncertainties: Omission of earlier chimeric receptor pioneers from the credited names may weaken an attribution.
Long-term durability and safety across indications is still being established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense correction of SMN2 splicing (nusinersen) converted spinal muscular atrophy, a leading genetic cause of infant death, into a treatable disease and validated splice-modulating oligonucleotides as a therapeutic platform. Strong mechanistic clarity and patient benefit.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the splicing mechanism and ISS-N1 target; Bennett led antisense chemistry and clinical development. This is a tidy two-person configuration. Contributions from SMN gene discovery (Melki, Lefebvre) are outside this candidate's credit.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with several years of real-world and trial data; recognition is timely though some argue the platform's broader reach is still unfolding.
uncertainties: The relative weight of the gene-discovery work versus therapeutic discovery is a boundary question.
Long-term outcome data in adults and later-treated patients is still maturing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Demonstrating TNF as a dominant driver in rheumatoid arthritis and showing clinical benefit of blockade established the cytokine-targeted paradigm for chronic inflammatory disease, with major use across arthritis, IBD and psoriasis. Impact on patient care is large and the logic is clear.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini are the central scientific and clinical pair with a clean two-person credit. Industrial antibody engineering and prior TNF biology (e.g. Cerami, Beutler) are outside the credit and could be argued as precedents.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of confirmation, biosimilars, and mechanism-informed follow-ons; fully mature, arguably overdue. My own field is close to this candidate, but I record no documented involvement and rank it on the common criteria.
uncertainties: Potential perception of field proximity; no documented personal tie is known to me.
Priority relative to earlier TNF biology researchers is debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway identified how cytosolic DNA is sensed and triggers interferon responses, linking innate immunity to infection, autoimmunity (e.g. interferonopathies, lupus), and cancer immunity. Conceptually original and highly generative.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the second messenger cGAMP; Barber discovered STING; Ishikawa shares STING discovery credit and Sun and Wu are co-authors on the cGAS work. A two-person split is defensible but leaves Ishikawa and others contested.
assessment.maturity: About a decade old with strong independent confirmation of mechanism; therapeutic translation in autoimmune disease and oncology is still emerging, which makes timing somewhat early.
uncertainties: Credit among Barber, Ishikawa, Chen and co-authors is not fully settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Molecular cloning of the T-cell receptor solved the long-standing problem of T-cell antigen recognition and underpins modern immunology, including TCR therapies and CAR design. The discovery is foundational and unambiguous in importance.
assessment.attribution: Davis/Hedrick and Mak/Yanagi cloned TCR genes essentially simultaneously in 1984; naming two leaders from the two groups is plausible, but excluding Hedrick and Yanagi is a real allocation problem.
assessment.maturity: Long established, with decades of confirmation; recognition is overdue, with the main barrier being attribution rather than maturity.
uncertainties: Concurrent discovery by two groups complicates a three-person limit.
Whether the Nobel committee views this as already covered by prior MHC and immune-recognition prizes is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL11A as the repressor of fetal hemoglobin explained the hemoglobin switch and, via genome-editing reactivation, led to an approved therapy for sickle cell disease and beta-thalassemia. Excellent combination of human genetics, mechanism and therapy.
assessment.attribution: Thein's genetic association work, Orkin and Sankaran's identification and functional validation of BCL11A, and Bauer's enhancer editing translation are all central; four credited names with a hard split.
assessment.maturity: Therapy approved only recently (2023), so clinical follow-up is short; mechanistic validation is strong and independently replicated.
uncertainties: Long-term safety and access outcomes of the editing therapy are not yet known.
Allocation between GWAS, mechanism, and editing translation is unresolved.
